intended_object: The subgradient image of a set s under an extended-real function f: ∂f(s) = ⋃_{x ∈ s} ∂f(x), the set of all subgradients of f at points of s, taken with respect to a bilinear pairing ⟪·,·⟫ between E and F. This comes from the docstring and the module documentation; it is the standard notion from Rockafellar, used for example for Monge–Ampère measures.
explanation:
The body is `⋃ x ∈ s, subdifferential B f x`, which is literally ∂f(s) = ⋃_{x∈s} ∂f(x). The underlying `subdifferential` is the standard one for extended-real functions:
- f x must be finite;
- f x + ⟪x' − x, y⟫ ≤ f x' must hold for every x'.

Requiring finiteness is the usual convention: the subdifferential is empty wherever f is ±∞. Degenerate cases also behave correctly: the image of the empty set is empty, and a point where f is infinite contributes nothing.

The generality is natural. E and F are arbitrary real vector spaces linked by an arbitrary bilinear pairing B, which includes the dual pairing and inner products. This is the setting of Rockafellar and of Ekeland–Témam.

I searched Mathlib for a definition of a subdifferential or subgradient (`subdifferential`, `SubderivAt`, `subgradient`, `HasSubgradient`, case-insensitive) and found none, so there is no more general counterpart to cite.
